definition: The naming system of the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry, which builds a compound's name from its parent chain, prefixes for branches and halogens, a suffix for the functional group, and locant numbers.
The longest continuous chain of carbon atoms that contains the main functional group (and any C=C bond); its length gives the stem of the name.
One of two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but atoms joined in a different order, such as butane and 2-methylpropane.

Classes of alcohols and halogenoalkanes set by how many carbon atoms are bonded to the carbon holding the OH or halogen (one or none, two, three); for amines, by how many carbon atoms are bonded to the nitrogen.
